meta.title: How it works
meta.description: How a question becomes an answer, why the sources are retrieved rather than remembered, and when the system declines to answer.

heading: How a question becomes a cited answer
standfirst: This page is for two readers: someone assessing the engineering, and someone deciding whether to trust an answer it gave them. It is the only page here that uses technical vocabulary, and it is the only page that describes machinery rather than law.

status.heading: What is actually built
status.body: Every stage below now runs. What most of them still run over is a small set of demonstration sources, because no document has been ingested — so they are marked as built on illustrative data rather than as finished. Each stage carries its own state, nothing here is written in the present tense unless the code does it today, and translation is marked unbuilt because returning text unchanged is not translating it. The one thing that would make this page useless is describing an ambition as a capability.

pipeline.heading: What happens to a question
pipeline.standfirst: Thirteen stages. Select one to see what it does, what it hands on, and what happens when it fails. Nothing advances on a timer.

detect.name: Language detection
detect.does: Works out which of the six supported languages the question is in, with a confidence score.
detect.outputs: A language code and a confidence, both shown in the interface so the reader can correct them.
detect.fails: A wrong guess is visible and correctable rather than silent. Below a confidence floor it asks instead of guessing.

understand.name: Query understanding
understand.does: Extracts what is being asked: intent, which rights are in play, which regulatory areas, hints about the product class, and named entities such as herbs, dosage forms and destination markets.
understand.outputs: A structured query, plus a decision on whether the question can be answered at all without more facts.
understand.fails: An ambiguous question routes to a clarifying question rather than to a confident answer about the wrong thing.

clarify.name: Clarify, if the class is undetermined
clarify.does: Where the answer depends on what the product is regulatorily and that is not yet known, asks the single most decisive question rather than answering for every possibility.
clarify.outputs: Either a product class, or an explicit statement that the answer is conditional on it.
clarify.fails: If the reader declines to answer, the system says which way the answer would turn rather than picking one.

route.name: Jurisdiction split
route.does: Selects the namespace to search. India and International are separate indexes, and a single retrieval call reads one of them.
route.outputs: A namespace, or two retrievals for a cross-border question.
route.fails: There is no fallback that merges the two. A question that cannot be routed is asked which jurisdiction it means.

retrieve.name: Retrieval
retrieve.does: Hybrid search over the selected namespace: keyword matching and dense vectors, fused. Metadata filters are applied before scoring — jurisdiction, effective date window, document type, product class and topic — so superseded text is never a candidate.
retrieve.outputs: A candidate set of passages with their scores and metadata.
retrieve.fails: Below a retrieval floor there is nothing to answer from, and the pipeline goes to abstention rather than to generation.

rerank.name: Reranking
rerank.does: A cross-encoder reads each candidate against the question and reorders them, cutting a broad candidate set down to the few that actually bear on it.
rerank.outputs: A short ranked list, carrying both the retrieval score and the rerank score.
rerank.fails: If nothing clears the rerank threshold, that is itself a signal, and confidence drops or the system abstains.

context.name: Context assembly
context.does: Packs the chosen passages with their metadata headers — title, section path, version, effective date — so the model can attribute what it uses. The token budget is enforced with document diversity, so the window is never filled from a single document.
context.outputs: A context block where every passage is addressable by id.
context.fails: If diversity cannot be met, the answer is marked as resting on a single source, which caps its confidence.

generate.name: Generation
generate.does: Answers from the provided passages and nothing else, under a prompt that forbids stating anything not present in them. Output is schema-constrained: the four blocks, plus a machine-readable map from each claim to the passages supporting it.
generate.outputs: Structured blocks and a claim-to-passage map, never prose to be parsed afterwards.
generate.fails: If the passages do not support an answer, the model is required to return an abstention object rather than its best guess.

map.name: Citation mapping
map.does: Checks every passage id the model returned against the passages actually supplied. Any claim whose citation does not verify is dropped.
map.outputs: An answer where every marker resolves to a real retrieved passage.
map.fails: If too many claims drop, the answer is downgraded or abstains. An uncited answer is never shown in place of a cited one.

confidence.name: Confidence scoring
confidence.does: Computes high, moderate, low or abstain from the retrieval result — how many passages cleared the threshold, how many distinct documents they came from, whether they contradict each other, and whether they are all within their effective window.
confidence.outputs: A level and a one-sentence reason, both shown.
confidence.fails: Records never raise or lower it. Confidence is a property of the sources, not of how the answer reads.

abstain.name: Abstention check
abstain.does: The last gate before an answer is shown. Decides whether the question was out of scope, whether the sources conflict, whether they are out of date, or whether nothing relevant was found.
abstain.outputs: Either an answer, or one of the abstention states below with what the reader is offered next.
abstain.fails: This is the stage that is allowed to fail loudly. Abstaining is a correct outcome, not an error.

translate.name: Translation
translate.does: Translates the answer into the reader's language, behind an interface so the implementation can be swapped — including for national language infrastructure.
translate.outputs: A translated answer with untranslated citation metadata.
translate.fails: Source passages are never translated. A translated citation is no longer a citation, and a reader checking a source needs the words as published.

render.name: The answer, with its sources
render.does: Renders the four blocks with claim-level markers, the confidence and its reason, and the source cards behind them. Sentences resting on no passage are marked as general explanation.
render.outputs: What you see on the workspace: an answer whose every marker resolves to a passage you can open and read in the words it was published in.
render.fails: If citation mapping produced nothing to show, this surface renders an abstention rather than an unsourced answer.

retrieval.heading: Why the sources are retrieved rather than remembered
retrieval.body1: A language model asked a legal question from its training data answers from memory. That answer is undated, unattributed, and confidently wrong on anything that has been amended since the model was trained — which, in this field, is a great deal. It cannot tell you where it got something, because it does not know.
retrieval.body2: Retrieval changes what the model is allowed to use. The answer is constrained to a curated, version-tracked set of published documents, each claim points at the passage behind it, and every answer carries the date of the sources it used.
retrieval.body3: It reduces hallucination and localises it. It does not eliminate it. A model can still misread a passage, or state something the passage does not quite say. That is precisely why every claim is checkable against the passage it names, why sentences resting on nothing are marked as such, and why the system is built to abstain rather than to produce something plausible.

abstention.heading: Declining to answer is a feature
abstention.standfirst: Most of the work in a product like this is in knowing when not to answer. These are the states, with what each one offers the reader next. The logic behind them is designed and not yet built; what you see here is the surface it will use.

nothing.title: Nothing relevant found
nothing.body: I couldn't find anything in these sources that answers this reliably.
nothing.offers: Rephrase, narrow the jurisdiction, name the product type, see what's covered, or send the question to a human with the context already filled in.

scope.title: Outside what this covers
scope.body: This is outside what I can answer. I cover intellectual property and regulatory requirements for Ayurvedic products — not clinical advice, individual legal opinions, or predictions about whether an application will succeed.
scope.offers: A plain statement of what it can do instead, and the escalation route.

conflict.title: The sources disagree
conflict.body: Two passages point different ways, and the answer depends on which governs.
conflict.offers: Both passages, with their dates and their documents, so the reader can see the disagreement rather than being handed one side of it.

stale.title: The sources may be out of date
stale.body: What was found sits outside its effective window, or predates an amendment the corpus knows about.
stale.offers: The passage with its date shown, and a plain statement that the position may have changed.

facts.title: It depends on facts you have not given
facts.body: The answer turns on something only you know — usually what the product is regulatorily.
facts.offers: The single most decisive question, rather than a list of every possibility.

jurisdictions.heading: Two namespaces, never merged
jurisdictions.body: India and International are separate indexes. A retrieval call reads one of them, and a cross-border question runs two retrievals and produces two answers rather than one blended paragraph. The reason is not tidiness: an answer that mixes the Indian position with an export market's is wrong in a way that reads as right, and a reader acting on it would not be able to tell which half applied to them.
jurisdictions.note: These two answers were produced separately and are shown side by side. Nothing in the product merges them, and no interface anywhere presents a single answer covering both.

architecture.heading: How it is put together
architecture.standfirst: Layers, and what state each part is in. The retriever's metadata filters are listed because they are what makes superseded text unreachable rather than merely deprioritised.
architecture.filters: Jurisdiction · product class · IP right · regulatory area · effective date window · document type · language
architecture.notScheduledBody: A knowledge graph over entities and provisions, agentic orchestration across several sources for one question, and connectors to subscription databases. These are directions, not commitments, and none of them is being built.

evaluation.heading: How it is measured
evaluation.standfirst: These are the axes it will be scored on. Two of them have a target of one hundred per cent, because a single failure on either is the kind that destroys trust in everything else.
evaluation.notRunBody: There is no corpus to retrieve from and no pipeline to score, so there are no numbers on this page. When the harness runs it will write a summary that this page reads, and whatever it says will appear here — including the bad numbers. A page of metric definitions with no results is less impressive than a table of figures, and considerably more honest.

answerAccuracy.name: Answer accuracy
answerAccuracy.what: Whether the answer is right, judged against a reference answer and spot-checked by a person.
answerAccuracy.target: as high as the sources allow

citationCorrectness.name: Citation correctness
citationCorrectness.what: Whether the passage a claim cites actually supports that claim.

citationValidity.name: Citation validity
citationValidity.what: Whether every citation resolves to a real, current passage.

abstentionPrecision.name: Abstention precision
abstentionPrecision.what: When it declines, whether it was right to.

abstentionRecall.name: Abstention recall
abstentionRecall.what: Whether it answers the questions it should answer, rather than declining defensively.

jurisdictionPurity.name: Jurisdiction purity
jurisdictionPurity.what: Whether any answer mixes the Indian position with another jurisdiction's.

authorityPurity.name: Authority purity
authorityPurity.what: Whether a filed or granted record ever appeared as a citation.

classificationAccuracy.name: Classification accuracy
classificationAccuracy.what: Whether the product class the flow reaches is the right one.

multilingualQuality.name: Multilingual quality
multilingualQuality.what: Whether an answer in Telugu is as good as the same answer in English, judged by a speaker.

latency.name: Latency
latency.what: How long an answer takes, at the median and at the tail.
